fullPassage: Analogies can serve two different functions in philosophy. Sometimes, as seems often the case in Plato, for example, they serve simply to illustrate. When Socrates compares the Good with the sun, he may simply be using the image of the sun to help bring to life his arguments about the Good. On other occasions, however, the analogy can be an integral part of an argument. Consider one of the most popular arguments for the existence of God, the 'argument from design', which has been advanced by many thinkers, from the ancient Stoics to British theologian William Paley. The argument holds that just as an artefact such as a watch implies the existence of an artisan, so the universe implies the existence of a divine creator. Here the analogy with the watch is not meant simply to illustrate a point. Rather, the analogy is supposed to show why we should conclude that the universe has a creator.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 유추는 철학에서 두 가지 다른 기능(functions)을 합니다. 단순히 예시를 들어 설명(illustrate)하기도 하며, 소크라테스는 태양의 이미지(image)를 사용합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ functions — illustrate — image: 원문과 정확히 일치
❌ ② problems(문제)는 functions(기능)과 다른 의미
❌ ③ complicate(복잡하게 하다)는 illustrate(설명하다)의 반의어
❌ ① analysis(분석)는 image(이미지)와 다른 개념
det.tip: serve two different functions = 두 가지 다른 기능을 하다. illustrate = 예시로 설명하다

det.tip: integral part = 필수적인 부분. advanced by = ~에 의해 주장된

det.tip: artefact = 인공물. implies = 암시하다. conclude = 결론짓다

det.korean: ①integral(필수적인), ②advanced(주장된), ③illustrate(설명하다)는 원문과 일치합니다. ④reject(거부하다)는 원문의 conclude(결론짓다)를 반의어로 교체한 것입니다.

questions.passage:
Analogies can serve two different functions in philosophy. Sometimes, as seems often the case in Plato, for example, they serve simply to illustrate. When Socrates compares the Good with the sun, he may simply be using the image of the sun to help bring to life his arguments about the Good. On other occasions, however, the analogy can be an integral part of an argument. Consider one of the most popular arguments for the existence of God, the 'argument from design', which has been advanced by many thinkers, from the ancient Stoics to British theologian William Paley. The argument holds that just as an artefact such as a watch implies the existence of an artisan, so the universe implies the existence of a divine creator. Here the analogy with the watch is not meant simply to illustrate a point. Rather, the analogy is supposed to show why we should ____ that the universe has a creator.

* analogy ** theologian *** artisan

✅ ① conclude(결론짓다): 원문 그대로. 설계 논증의 목적
❌ ④ deny(부정하다): 논증의 목적과 정반대
❌ ② question(의문을 품다): 결론이 아닌 의심
❌ ③ ignore(무시하다): 논증의 목적과 무관
det.tip: conclude that = ~라고 결론짓다. 설계 논증은 우주에 창조자가 있다는 결론을 유도
